referents.why: 'His hand' is Aaron's, the subject of the act (third masculine singular).
'It covered the land' is third feminine singular, and the frogs are the feminine singular subject of the verse.

links.why: A then-link runs within a verse only. The narrative line here continues from the frame of the speech, a cross-verse sequence that is not a link type.
Aaron's stretching out brings about the frogs' coming up, so the relation is an outcome, not a sequence.
Aaron stretched out his hand, and the frogs came up: what the act brings about.
A wayyiqtol with the same subject continues the narrative within the verse: came up, then covered.

groups.why: A command to stretch out the hand, then the same verb reported as done by Aaron. There is no pro-form such as 'did so'. Proposed as a reading for review (R5).
groups.category: command then the same act reported

none_fit.what: A sequence across verses has no link type: then is within a verse only, and the episode rung is not in link_types.

cant_tell.what: Whether 'the frogs came up' (cl1) fulfils the command 'bring up the frogs' (Exo.8.1 cl3).
cant_tell.why: Same root but qal rather than hiphil, and no 'did so' report; left unlinked.
